text:
jordan: Hi team — customer ACME (acme-inc) escalated: invoice INV-2026-0443 shows 4,200,312 tokens billed but our dashboard served_tokens ~2,108,944. They run continuous batching (batch_window_ms=100) + KV cache. Trace attached (trace-0a1b2c). Can someone triage?

maria: Thanks Jordan. Can you paste tenant id + a few request ids or a sample trace? Also which model and timeframe?

jordan: tenant: acme-inc
trace: trace-0a1b2c
timeframe: 2026-04-11 00:00-04:00 UTC
model: rdx-13b-quant-v2
sample request payload:
```
{"prompt": "Summarize...", "max_tokens": 256, "stream": false}
```
We also have a replay log snippet where we see differing counters:
```
metering.tokens_billed=1200
serve.tokens_sent=600
cache.kv_hits=550
```
Looks like billed ~= sent + ... but numbers don't add up.

alex: Quick explainer: we currently increment metered token counters at batch formation time. Continuous batching sometimes merges requests with different prefix lengths; the runtime may account tokens per-request before applying prefix/KV cache de-dup at the model call. So billed_tokens can reflect duplicated prefix tokens across batched logical requests even if cache short-circuits the model execution. Also there is rounding when batching merges partial windows. Key logs to look for: `metering.tokens_billed`, `serve.tokens_sent`, `cache.kv_hits`, `batch.window_ms`, `batch.request_count`.

chris: Repro plan:
1) Enable debug: `export RW_BATCH_DEBUG=1`
2) Run the replay tool in simulate mode: `./tools/replay --tenant acme-inc --trace trace-0a1b2c --simulate-continuous`
3) Collect /var/log/redwood/runtime.log and grep for `metering.` and `cache.` keys.
Example commands:
```
RW_BATCH_DEBUG=1 ./tools/replay --tenant acme-inc --trace trace-0a1b2c --simulate-continuous | tee replay.out
grep -E "metering\.|cache\." replay.out
```

jordan: Did the replay; attaching snippet:
```
[2026-04-11T00:12:03Z] batch.id=bd-77 batch.window_ms=100 batch.request_count=3
[2026-04-11T00:12:03Z] request.id=r-100 metering.tokens_billed=900 serve.tokens_sent=300 cache.kv_hits=580
[2026-04-11T00:12:03Z] request.id=r-101 metering.tokens_billed=900 serve.tokens_sent=300 cache.kv_hits=580
```
So two requests show same billed tokens even though serve.tokens_sent is much smaller. That suggests per-request billing duplicated the long prefix at batch time.

alex: Yup — this is the bug category. Metering should subtract `cache.kv_hits` (or charge only unique model tokens) at billing time. We debated this before because removing billed duplication interacts with committed capacity and reserved accounting. Short term we can credit the account for the delta.

maria: For customer-facing fix: I propose issuing a partial credit equal to (sum(metering.tokens_billed) - sum(serve.tokens_sent)). Need approvals for credits > $5k. Finance: can you chime in?

sara: From product: disabling continuous batching per-account is low risk but may increase latency/cost for ACME. We need to surface tradeoffs in the ticket before flipping any flags.

chris: Mitigation steps:
- Create ticket CUST-9876 and attach logs and replay output.
- Propose temporary config `disable_continuous_batching=true` for acme-inc while we patch metering.
- Small patch to metering: apply `billed = billed - min(cache.kv_hits, billed)` for continuous batches (targeted rollout).
Timeline: repro today, patch in staging by EOD, rollout next week.

support_bot: Ticket created: #CUST-9876 — assigned to @jordan and @alex :ticket:

jordan: I'll attach the replay outputs and customer invoice, and request a pre-approval for credits. Thanks all :thumbsup:

maria: Also please attach the `batch.id` values for the window so finance can map to bytes invoiced.

jordan: Will do. Filing now.
